caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular quilt or textile piece with a white or light cream background. The primary design elements are red starburst or flower-like shapes, each with multiple pointed petals arranged radially around a central circular area. These shapes are evenly spaced in a grid pattern. The quilt is bordered by a geometric edge composed of alternating red and white triangles forming a sawtooth pattern along both the visible horizontal and vertical edges. Inside the border, there are faintly sketched circular and floral motifs as part of the overall pattern, adding additional texture within the background. The drawing includes a representation of the quilt with one corner folded over, revealing the continuous edge pattern on both the front and reverse. At the bottom, there is a scale indicator marked at 2 feet 4 inches. The name “John Ritowers” and the notation “DEL. 133” are inscribed in the lower right corner.
title: Quilted Applique Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
